punchline: A sign in a national park saying many people take petrified wood led visitors to take nearly three times as much.
thirty_sec: A park in Arizona wanted visitors to stop taking petrified wood, so it posted a sign saying many people did. Robert Cialdini's team marked pieces of wood and counted: nearly three times as many vanished as on a path with no sign. A plain request not to remove any worked better. His book Influence calls this negative social proof.
